- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.10) and price is trending upward, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid premature reversal.  
- Model frequently underestimates late-period spikes (especially after 20–25 days horizon) — apply a 2–5% upward bias for the final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing sentiment-driven reversals — if sentiment turns sharply positive after 10 days, adjust forecast to rise 1–3% above prior 7-day average.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 5%+ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- Overshoot after spikes: if model peaks 10%+ above recent high, reduce by 5–10% in next 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms continuation.
